skill.name: herdr
skill.description: Control Herdr, a terminal multiplexer for coding agents. Use only when the user explicitly mentions Herdr or asks to use Herdr to inspect or control panes, tabs, workspaces, commands, or another agent. Do not use merely because a task could benefit from a background terminal, delegation, or parallel work. Requires HERDR_ENV=1.
skill.summary: Control Herdr terminal layouts, coding agents, commands, and pane output from a managed session.
skill.author: herdrdev

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code being mistaken for Ruby backtick execution. Seven examples perform real Herdr mutations, including launching agents, sending input, changing layout, and running a shell command; these capabilities are expected but require deliberate targeting.

remediation.issue: The pane run workflow can execute arbitrary command text in another shell.
remediation.suggestion: Run only commands explicitly requested by the user, preserve argument boundaries, and request confirmation before destructive or privileged operations.

remediation.issue: Agent start, prompt, send-keys, and pane split commands can alter active work or launch resource-consuming processes.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the Herdr environment preflight, resolve explicit pane or agent targets, and confirm ambiguous mutations before execution.

content.user_title: Control Herdr Workspaces and Coding Agents
content.value_statement: Managing several coding agents across terminal panes can make state, focus, and output difficult to track. This skill uses Herdr commands to organize panes, coordinate agents, run commands, and inspect results.
actual_capabilities: Verifies that the current process is running inside a Herdr-managed pane.
Lists workspaces, tabs, panes, and coding agents while reading stable identifiers from responses.
Splits panes while preserving the current directory and user focus.
Starts supported coding agents, sends prompts or keys, and waits for lifecycle changes.
Runs ordinary terminal commands in sibling panes and waits for matching output.
Reads visible, recent, unwrapped, or detection-focused pane output.
limitations: Requires HERDR_ENV=1 and an installed herdr binary in PATH.
Controls only the current Herdr session from a Herdr-managed pane.
Cannot recover output that has already left a terminal alternate screen.
Depends on the installed CLI syntax and locally supported agent kinds.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a code review
use_cases.description: Create a sibling pane, start a reviewer agent, send the review request, and collect actionable findings.

use_cases.title: Run tests beside active work
use_cases.description: Open a background pane, run the requested test command, wait for completion text, and inspect recent output.

use_cases.title: Inspect parallel agent progress
use_cases.description: List active agents, check lifecycle states, and read output without changing the user interface focus.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the current session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Herdr to list the current workspace, tabs, panes, and agents. Summarize their identifiers and states without changing focus.

prompt_templates.title: Run a background test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Herdr to create a sibling pane in the current directory. Run [test command], wait for completion, and summarize the output.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate a focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Herdr to start a [agent kind] agent named [name] in a sibling pane. Ask it to review [scope] and return actionable findings.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate parallel investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Herdr to start two named agents for [task A] and [task B]. Preserve focus, monitor both, and consolidate their verified results.

output_examples.input: Use Herdr to inspect the current session without changing focus.
output: Two panes are available, with one idle coding agent.

output_examples.input: Use Herdr to run the project tests in a sibling pane and summarize the result.
output_examples.output: The tests completed in a background pane. All 48 tests passed, and the user focus remained in the original pane.

output_examples.input: Use Herdr to ask a reviewer agent for actionable findings.
output_examples.output: The reviewer reached a settled state and reported two actionable findings concerning timeout handling and missing error-path coverage.

best_practices: Verify HERDR_ENV before issuing any Herdr control command.
Use explicit pane identifiers or unique agent names, and parse identifiers from command responses.
Preserve the current directory and user focus unless the user requests a different layout.
anti_patterns: Do not invoke Herdr unless the user explicitly requests Herdr.
Do not guess identifiers or rely on another client focus.
Do not close sessions or stop servers without explicit user authorization.

faq.question: What must be installed before using this skill?
faq.answer: The herdr binary must be available in PATH, and the current process must have HERDR_ENV set to 1.

faq.question: Can this skill control Herdr from outside a managed pane?
faq.answer: No. The skill stops when the Herdr environment check fails.

faq.question: Can it start Claude, Codex, or Claude Code agents?
faq.answer: It can start agent kinds supported by the installed Herdr version. The requested kind must be locally available.

faq.question: Does it keep the current terminal focus?
faq.answer: Yes, background workflows use no-focus controls unless the user requests a focus change.

faq.question: Can it run ordinary shell commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run requested command text in a selected pane, wait for output, and read the result.

faq.question: How does it handle blocked agents?
faq.answer: It inspects the agent state and recent output before sending deliberate keys or additional input.
